items.claim: The row's two supporting textual claims for the 4:20 opening — the bni-opening ordinal and the unbroken-imperative-mood argument — are both byte-false, though the seam itself still holds on other grounds.
items.evidence: prov_device_inventory.json's bni_address list places five, not four, vocative beni occurrences inside the Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 span this row's ordinal claim covers: oshb:Prov.3.1, oshb:Prov.3.11, oshb:Prov.3.21, oshb:Prov.4.10, oshb:Prov.4.20. The row's own boundary_evidence_refs and observed_substrate_signals omit oshb:Prov.3.11, undercounting oshb:Prov.4.20 (“בְּ֭נִי…”) as the 'fourth' opener when the inventory shows it is the fifth. Separately, the rejected_alternative claims the second-person address and imperative mood 'carry unbroken from 4.20 through 4.27,' but oshb:Prov.4.22 (“כִּֽי חַיִּ֣ים הֵ֭ם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶ֑ם וּֽלְכָל בְּשָׂר֥וֹ מַרְפֵּֽא”; web:Prov.4.22 “For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.”) is a third-person כי-motive clause with no second-person address or imperative verb, breaking the claimed run. Neither error defeats the 4:20 opening itself (the address-formula recurrence and the external oshb:Prov.4.19 petuchah still hold), but both weaken the row's own stated grounds for rejecting a cut after 4:22.

items.claim: The 5:1 vocative opening and the 5:6 negated-knowledge closing jointly carry both boundaries of this instruction_lecture, and the rejected alternative engages the real rival rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.5.1 (“בְּ֭נִי”) and its imperative open the unit on the singular address; oshb:Prov.5.6's closing clause (“תֵדָֽע”, 'she doesn't know it') negates the very discernment the opening commends, and oshb:Prov.5.7's plural (“וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ”) reopens address on a distinct vocative number immediately after — a real register/number shift, not a strawman rejection of the 5:1-14 extension. All curly WEB quotes in this row verified byte-verbatim (check_web_quotes.py, GREEN); the oshb:Prov.5.6 petuchah is disclosed as tier-3 single-witness corroboration only, not the driver.

items.claim: The plural-vocative reopening at 5:7 and the first-person confession closing at 5:14 correctly bound this unit, and the parashah-silence disclosure across 5:7-14 checks out against the inventory.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.5.7 (“וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ”) is a genuine number/register shift from the singular beni of 5:1; the quoted confession at web:Prov.5.14 (“I have come to the brink of utter ruin, among the gathered assembly.””) is byte-verbatim (check_web_quotes.py, GREEN). pmarks_Prov.json carries no PE/SAMEKH entry between Prov.5.7 and Prov.5.14, matching the row's own disclosure that no parashah mark corroborates this internal seam. The rejected alternative (one continuous chapter-lecture) is a real, commonly-held rival, correctly set aside on the register shift at 5:15.

items.claim: The row's own back seam (5:19/5:20) carries an undisclosed byte-true catchword — the verb-root shagah repeated verbatim across the boundary — that the cross-seam-cohesion rule requires surfacing.
items.evidence: consonantal_index.json's skeleton tier shows oshb:Prov.5.19 (this row's own last verse) closes with “תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד” and oshb:Prov.5.20 (the immediately following row) opens its rhetorical question with the same root (“וְלָ֤מָּה תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה בְנִ֣י”); WEB itself renders both occurrences with the identical English verb (web:Prov.5.19 “A loving doe and a graceful deer— let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.”; web:Prov.5.20 “For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?”). This is a real lexical link straddling the row's own seam, not merely a shared theme, and it is not named in boundary_evidence_refs or device_notes for either adjoining row. It does not by itself overturn the register shift (blessing/imperative vs. rhetorical question) the row argues, but it is exactly the undisclosed cross-seam device the governing rules require disclosing.

items.claim: The row's own front seam (5:19/5:20) shares the identical undisclosed shagah catchword with the preceding row, and the row also misses that the same root closes its own span at 5:23, forming an inclusio it never names.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.5.20 opens with “וְלָ֤מָּה תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה” and oshb:Prov.5.23, this row's own closing verse, ends with “יִשְׁגֶּֽה” — the identical root shagah bracketing 5:20-5:23 (web:Prov.5.20 “For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?”; web:Prov.5.23 “He will die for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will go astray.”), a genuine inclusio device never named in device_notes even though device_notes otherwise catalogs the unit's parallelism texture. The same root also closes the immediately preceding verse, oshb:Prov.5.19 (“תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד”, web:Prov.5.19 “A loving doe and a graceful deer— let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.”), an undisclosed cross-seam link at the row's own front boundary. Disclosure, not the boundary call, is the defect: the mid-verse vocative shift at 5:20 and the petuchah at 5:23 still argue the seams as claimed.

items.claim: The 6:1 vocative-plus-conditional opening and the 6:6 addressee-type change to an unnamed sluggard correctly bound this admonition_unit, and the paseq/petuchah disclosures at 6:3 and 6:5 are accurate.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.6.1 (“בְּ֭נִי אִם עָרַ֣בְתָּ…”) opens on a distinct topic (suretyship) and second-person conditional address; pmarks_Prov.json confirms a paseq at Prov.6.3 and a petuchah (PE) at Prov.6.5, both correctly disclosed as count/position-limited (paseq) and single-witness tier-3 (petuchah). oshb:Prov.6.6 (“לֵֽךְ אֶל נְמָלָ֥ה עָצֵ֑ל”) opens on a wholly different addressee-type, matching the row's own rejected-alternative reasoning against merging forward. All Hebrew quotes in the row byte-verified against verse_map_oshb.json and WEB quotes verbatim (check_web_quotes.py, GREEN).

items.claim: The rejected_alternative compares this admonition_unit to the book's wisdom_poem spans, an easily-dismissed strawman that skips the real live rival: whether the third-person ant illustration should split from the direct sluggard address that resumes at 6:9.
items.evidence: No reader would seriously classify 6:6-11 as wisdom_poem given its second-person imperative/interrogative address against the third-person hymnic voice of 1:20-33/ch.8/ch.9 — the row's own stated reason for rejecting it, which makes the comparison a strawman rather than the strongest real rival. The genuinely competing boundary question, left untested: oshb:Prov.6.7 (“אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֵֽין לָ֥הּ קָצִ֗ין שֹׁטֵ֥ר וּמֹשֵֽׁל”) and oshb:Prov.6.8 (“תָּכִ֣ין בַּקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָ֑הּ אָגְרָ֥ה בַ֝קָּצִ֗יר מַאֲכָלָֽהּ”) describe the ant in the third person before oshb:Prov.6.9 (“עַד מָתַ֖י עָצֵ֥ל…”) returns to direct second-person address of the sluggard — a real internal-seam candidate the row never engages, nor does it test merging with the adjoining 6:1-5 admonition_unit as one longer interlude. The petuchah/paseq disclosures at 6:5, 6:9-6:10, and 6:11 are otherwise accurate, and this does not challenge the row's final span or unit_type.

items.claim: The shared-subject participial chain across 6:12-6:15, closed by the causal consequence clause, is byte-grounded cluster cohesion, and both named rivals (admonition_unit, single_proverb) are the real competing categories in the closed vocabulary, correctly rejected.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.6.12's nominal opener (“אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה”) governs the third-person participial chain through oshb:Prov.6.14 (“תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ חֹרֵ֣שׁ רָ֣ע בְּכָל עֵ֑ת מדנים מִדְיָנִ֥ים יְשַׁלֵּֽחַ”), and oshb:Prov.6.15's causal opener (“עַל כֵּ֗ן”) draws the consequence from that one accumulated subject — a construction-run form of cohesion the granularity policy accepts in place of a shared token. Both Hebrew quotes byte-verified against verse_map_oshb.json. The row correctly rejects admonition_unit (no second-person imperative address here, unlike its neighbors at 6:1-5/6:6-11) and single_proverb (cohesion spans four verses, not a couplet) as the two real live alternatives in the closed vocabulary, and it accurately discloses the inline ketiv/qere at 6:14 as a spelling note (matching pmarks_Prov.json's kq entry for Prov.6.14), not a boundary signal.
